ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening of all UBOs, shareholders, directors, and authorized signatories against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council sanctions lists (1267/1988 and 2231 regimes), and the Luxembourg national financial-sanctions list maintained by the Ministry of Finance; OFAC SDN List screening required as enhanced-risk due diligence given USD-denominated payment rails (Stripe, Authorize.Net); mandatory PEP-status determination under Article 2 of the Law of 12 November 2004 and FATF Recommendation 12, including family members and close associates; continuous adverse-media monitoring; re-screening triggered by any change in ownership, ID expiry, or payment-rail change; all results documented in a written KYC file retained by the notary and the incorporating bank.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS), single online access via lbr.lu; incorporation name verification is effected by the Luxembourg notary against the RCS index before execution of the notarial deed
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names are accepted in Latin script in French, German, Luxembourgish, or English; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters; the corporate form suffix 'SARL' or 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' is mandatory; the name must be distinctive and non-misleading under Article 28 of the Law of 19 December 2002; false state affiliation or geographic exclusivity is rejected.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg (when falsely implying state or public authority connection)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name clearance is obtained through the notary's pre-verification at the RCS and is valid for 30 days pending execution of the notarial deed. Upon rejection, the notary immediately re-submits a new clearance request containing up to three alternative names. An administrative appeal may be filed with the Minister of Justice within 15 days of the rejection notice under Article 4 of the Law of 19 December 2002; judicial recourse lies to the administrative section of the Tribunal d'Arrondissement within three months. Typical counsel fees for an appeal are USD 500-1,000.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. Luxembourg permits domiciliation of a SARL at the address of a licensed domiciliation agent (law firm, auditor, or approved professional) under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies. However, for an ISIC 3240 collectible-trading-card manufacturing and publishing entity utilizing US payment rails, a purely virtual arrangement without any local staff or premises is high-risk under OECD BEPS Action 5 substance review, the ATAD/GAAR rules, and post-Pillar Two substance requirements. A serviced office with at least a one-person executive or local manager presence is strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 20-30% likelihood of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 24 months after incorporation, driven by Luxembourg's RBE verification program, FIU AML/CFT on-site inspection campaigns, and OECD substance-exchange reviews; the probability increases where the registered office is located in a shared domiciliation cluster.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) — competent authority for Luxembourg VAT registration, VAT returns and indirect tax enforcement; Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) — competent authority for Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; official digital portals: guichet.lu and MyGuichet.lu (business e-government single access point); electronic VAT filing and registration are processed through the AED e-filing module (eTVA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign investor forms the SARL before a Luxembourg notary, subscribes the fully paid minimum share capital of EUR 12,000, and files incorporation formalities with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS/LBR), which issues the business registration certificate, the RCS number and the national identification number. The SARL must then apply to the AED for VAT registration using Form 010/010D, filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu or the Entreprise Desk prior to commencing taxable activity; the AED issues the VAT identification number in the format LU + 8 digits. Non-established foreign suppliers without a Luxembourg permanent establishment must appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative and register directly with the AED, or alternatively use the Union OSS/IOSS simplification for distance sales and imports of low-value consignments. Social security registration (CCSS) and statistical registration (STATEC) follow concurrently. The VAT number must be quoted on all invoices, and the SARL must be entered in the Luxembourg VAT register before any deductible input VAT may be claimed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Luxembourg SARL is an opaque limited-liability company (société de capitaux) subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) and the solidarity surcharge (7% of CIT), for a combined headline CIT rate of approximately 24.94% in Luxembourg City. No pass-through, transparent treatment, or US-style check-the-box election is available for an SARL under Luxembourg domestic law. Resident SARLs are taxed on worldwide income where registered office and central administration are in Luxembourg; non-resident shareholders are not directly taxable on the SARL's profits until distributions occur, and dividend withholding rules apply separately. There is no tax-exempt free zone in Luxembourg; however, the participation exemption (100% exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains) and the IP box (80% exemption for qualifying IP income) constitute preferential regimes requiring substance and holding-period compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elective classification regime. Available statutory elections include: (i) VAT grouping election (assujetti unique) under Article 60 LTVAT for financially, economically and organisationally linked persons; (ii) waiver of the small-business VAT franchise so as to exercise input VAT deduction; (iii) corporate income tax consolidation election (intégration fiscale) under Article 164bis LIR for groups with direct or indirect shareholdings of at least 95% in Luxembourg-resident subsidiaries; (iv) qualification for the participation-exemption regime subject to a 12-month holding period and substance conditions; (v) mandatory application of ATAD 1 and ATAD 2 hybrid-mismatch rules (Law of 21 December 2017), which deny deductions for hybrid payments and contain no grandfathering or elective opt-out; (vi) ordinary regime elections such as the fixed-asset depreciation schedule and R&D tax credit options. Tax-exempt-zone elections do not exist in Luxembourg.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA) — Luxembourg national VAT system established by the Law of 12 February 1979 (LTVAT) as amended, implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover registration threshold for Luxembourg-established taxable persons: any person carrying out an independent economic activity in Luxembourg must register for VAT before commencing activity, regardless of projected turnover. A domestic small-business franchise exemption (Article 57 LTVAT) applies to annual VAT-exclusive turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000, but a taxable person established as an SARL may elect to waive the franchise and register normally. For non-established EU suppliers, intra-community distance sales to Luxembourg trigger registration when annual distance sales exceed EUR 100,000, unless the Union OSS scheme is used; for non-EU suppliers, VAT registration is generally required from the first taxable supply unless IOSS applies to low-value imports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently enforces no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based e-invoicing clearance regime for B2B transactions. Electronic invoicing to Luxembourg public-sector entities via the PEPPOL network is mandatory under EU Directive 2014/55/EU. B2B VAT invoices must be issued no later than the 15th day of the month following the taxable event and must contain the mandatory Article 57 LTVAT particulars; paper, PDF or structured EDI invoices are equally acceptable pending transposition of the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) package. Taxpayers must retain complete invoice trails, purchase ledgers, sales ledgers, and electronic audit files (SAF-T components) for AED inspection; future ViDA-derived e-invoicing and digital reporting obligations will apply upon national transposition.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Articles 39 and 40 LTVAT. Direct exports of tangible collectible trading cards dispatched or transported outside the EU by the supplier or on the supplier's behalf qualify for the 0% rate (Article 39). Intra-EU dispatches to a customer holding a valid VAT identification number in another Member State qualify for zero-rating under Article 40, subject to EC sales-list reporting, transport evidence, and the customer's VAT number appearing on the invoice. Export-linked services (e.g., printing, finishing, packaging and logistics) are zero-rated where they are performed directly for an EU/non-EU counterparty in connection with the goods placed outside the EU or temporarily moved within the EU, subject to the AED's documentation criteria. The burden of proof of physical exit and economic substance rests on the exporter; failure to substantiate the zero-rating converts the supply into a domestic Luxembourg supply taxed at 17%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/EX-A) or Exit Summary Declaration lodged through the Luxembourg/European e-customs system
Bill of Lading (sea), CMR consignment note (road), or Air Waybill (air) evidencing dispatch of the goods to a destination outside the EU
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the collectible trading cards, quantities, unit values, Incoterms and export customs classification codes (ISIC 3240 / corresponding HS code)
Purchase order, supply contract and transport instruction chain evidencing the foreign customer relationship and arm's-length pricing
Inward Remittance Certificate: bank SWIFT MT103 transfer advice or credit confirmation evidencing settlement of the export invoice and foreign-currency repatriation
EC Sales List (recapitulative statement) and Intrastat declarations, where the supply is an intra-EU dispatch rather than a direct export
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AED performs risk-based audit verification of zero-rated export claims, examining customs interfaces, transport contracts, terminal receipts, carrier statements and matching bank remittances. Where export status is not substantiated, the AED reassesses VAT at 17% with statutory monthly late interest, disallows the corresponding input VAT deduction and may impose administrative penalties on undeclared or misdeclared tax. Fraudulent export zero-rating — false customs declarations, fictitious transport documentation, circular payment schemes, or sham foreign customers — engages Articles 109 and 214 LTVAT and the Luxembourg Customs Code: criminal fines of up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment of up to five years in aggravated cases, joint and several liability of the gérant (managers), extension of the standard five-year assessment limitation period to ten years where fraud is established, retrospective clawback of all VAT and interest from the opening of the audit window, de-registration from VAT and OSS/IOSS schemes, and referral of money-laundering indicators to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit. Luxembourg imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; the 180-day inward-remittance benchmark set in this dossier serves as the banking, transfer-pricing and audit evidentiary standard for demonstrating genuine export consideration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting as the national central bank within the Eurosystem, with prudential control of credit institutions delegated by statute to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the BCL jointly; the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance retains policy oversight of the anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing (AML/CFT) legal framework, principally the Law of 12 November 2004, as amended.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Luxembourg franc was fully replaced by the euro (EUR) on 1 January 1999, and EUR is the sole legal tender; Luxembourg maintains complete current-account and capital-account convertibility, unimpeded by Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, which guarantees free movement of capital between Member States and third countries. No exchange-control authorization, capital-export license, advance approval, or foreign-investment screening applies to a SARL's profit remittance, dividend distribution, repayment of shareholder loans, intercompany treasury settlements, or the conversion of USD income into EUR. The only operational constraint is the standard documentary confirmation of the economic purpose of a transfer and, where relevant, BCL statistical reporting of cross-border direct-investment and intercompany financial flows for euro-area Balance of Payments (BoP) data under BCL Circular 2020/01 and related reporting instructions; the de minimis reporting threshold is generally EUR 12,500 per transaction, filed by the resident credit institution or corporate reporting unit.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender, mandatory conversion ratio, repatriation deadline, or foreign-currency holding restriction applies to a Luxembourg SARL. Invoicing for the collectible trading card business may be denominated freely in EUR, USD, or any other currency, and receipts may be retained in dedicated multi-currency operational accounts with eligible credit institutions. The only affirmative duties are: (i) accurate bookkeeping of trade receivables under Luxembourg GAAP or IFRS as elected; (ii) treatment of the proceeds for corporate income tax and VAT purposes at the calendar-year close; and (iii) submission of monthly/quarterly Intrastat and customs declarations for goods imported from and exported to EU and non-EU jurisdictions, administered by the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Agency (ADA).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating for offshore digital e-money institutions (EMIs) is Medium for merchant-acquiring settlement (e.g., PayPal (Europe) S.a r.l., Mangopay S.A., or EU-passported EMIs), but Low for the SARL's primary operating account. A Luxembourg-regulated payment institution or electronic money institution may open the account remotely, expedite onboarding, and provide direct integration with card acquirers; however, an EMI cannot grant credit, has narrower treasury product coverage, lacks documentary trade finance capacity, and the group treasury must still hold its irrevocable operational liquidity in a fully licensed credit institution to satisfy counterparty risk and notarial attestations. Legal constraints: CSSF authorization or passport notification, client-money safeguarding rules under the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services as amended, segregation of collected funds from the EMI's own insolvency estate, and absolute prohibition of credit extension by EMIs; accordingly, the recommended structure is a cross-border EMI for card settlement receiving rails (Stripe/Authorize.Net payouts) combined with a Tier-1 bank account for main cash concentration.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: An in-person KYC interview at the bank's office remains the prevailing norm, and at least one duly appointed manager (gérant) or a fully empowered director with board-secretary attestation must physically appear, together with a certified copy of the notarial deed of incorporation, Articles of Association, RBE certificate (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs), and passport copies. Remote account opening is technically permissible for a low-risk SARL if the bank's AML/CFT unit approves an exceptional remote onboarding protocol, but only with notarized and apostilled identity and corporate documents, a bank reference from the shareholder's existing regulated bank, and an online video verification interview generating a verifiable recording; most Luxembourg Tier-1 banks nevertheless reject 100% remote opening for a newly formed non-resident-managed SARL and will require a branch visit in Luxembourg, a meeting at the Luxembourg notary's office, or an appointment with a CESFE-certified introducer (e.g., an approved fiduciary or accounting firm).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: The SARL is majority owned by another corporate layer, or a UBO holding 25% or more cannot be identified with passport data and residency proof, including where an individual sits at the end of a foreign trust or nominee arrangement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete chain-of-title documentation from the RBE extract; signed UBO declaration form (bank specific); organizational chart with all intermediate holding vehicles; notarized declaration of the controlling shareholder disclosing the natural-person UBO; passport, proof of address, and CV of the ultimate individual; for any nominee, the underlying trust deed and registered corporate services act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds and source-of-wealth insufficiency for the initial EUR 12,000 minimum capital block, subsequent shareholder loans, or large international trade inbound payments from purchasers of collectible trading cards.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six-month bank statements of the funding entity; audited or management financial statements of the shareholder; sale/purchase agreement evidencing a genuine corporate transaction; notarized share subscription certificate; funds-flow explanation letter; VAT registration (LU number); invoice and customs bill of lading if trade-backed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume card-not-present (CNP) receivables: The Stripe/Authorize_Net channels create thousands of small consumer payments, and banks may flag the merchant-acquiring flow as a money mule or layering vehicle unless the payment processing logic is transparent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant account agreement and processing statistics; PCI-DSS attestation of compliance; data-processing contract; product catalogue and sample production invoices; refund policy document; consumer dispute resolution procedure; audited crime-risk mapping demonstrating the low-risk standard classification of collectible card publishing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk supplier corridors: purchase of holographic pressure-sensitive adhesive films, cold foil, card stock, and print modules from Chinese or Hong Kong intermediaries, including potential free-zone shell entities, triggers enhanced customer due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Due-diligence file on each offshore supplier: certificate of incorporation, VAT/equivalent tax number, business licence, bank confirmation, contractual terms, commercial invoice, packaging list, insurance certificate, and prior customs entries; evidence that payment beneficiaries are genuine industrial producers rather than cash-collection agents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance deficiency: the SARL is perceived as an empty shell with foreign non-resident managers, no Luxembourg office, no payroll, and no independent decision making, particularly where the board meets abroad.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Luxembourg lease or registered sub-lease for office/warehouse; letter from a Luxembourg service provider (fiduciary, accountant, or logistics agent); local payroll or service agreements with resident directors; Luxembourg corporate minutes; anticipated Luxembourg VAT and corporate tax filings; bank-facility utilization plan and carbon-copy of the business plan projecting local employment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for share-capital injection uses an irrevocable SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer where both banks are in SEPA) executed by the shareholder's bank, with instruction: beneficiary = 'LU_SARL', field 59 showing the exact legal name and IBAN (LU + 3-digit BIC of the receiving bank), field 72/remittance information containing 'SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION — LU_SARL — NOTARY DEED [date] — [notary file no.]', and the transaction classified as BOCODE 'S1.1 direct investment equity' in the BCL statistical declaration. The funds land in the blocked sub-account (compte d'attente / compte bloqué) bearing the notary's reference; the bank issues an attestation de blocage confirming the minimum EUR 12,000 is fully paid; the notary then draws on this attestation to execute the deed of incorporation, after which the bank converts the blocked account into an operational current account. For shareholder or intercompany loans, the inbound message must reference a signed intercompany loan agreement, bear the purpose code 'S1.4 direct investment intercompany loan', and, if cross-border and above the BCL threshold, be reported to the BCL BoP system; no central-bank approval is required, but the underlying documentation must be retained for the annual audit and CSSF AML files.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The preferred clearing rails are, first, SEPA Credit Transfer (pain.001 ISO 20022 XML) for routine EUR payments to EU suppliers of foil, ink, packaging and logistics; second, SWIFT MT103 for non-EU trades in EUR, USD or GBP, using the bank's correspondent network; third, irrevocable documentary letters of credit (UCP 600) for large purchases from China or Hong Kong, with MT700 issuance, involvement of the finance department in checking the shipping, insurance, and quality certificates against the LC terms, and MT202 COVER for the reimbursement if cross-currency; fourth, documentary collections (DP/DA, MT400/MT422) for recurring mid-value orders; and fifth, settlement of Stripe/Authorize.Net consumer receivables by merchant-payout or SWIFT USD transfer into the SARL's multi-currency account, with same-day value via Fedwire/CHIPS and subsequent customer-facing conversion only where the designated settlement currency is EUR. The treasury mandate requires the use of shared charges (SHA), exact matching of the beneficiary ABI/name in the MT103, invoicing with the SARL's LU VAT ID where applicable, and the archiving of all customs declarations and trade documents in the BCL statistical file for a five-year period.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD outright forward (plain vanilla deliverable forward), with maturities from spot to 24 months, commonly window-forwards matched to monthly Stripe/Authorize.Net settlement cycles
EUR/USD foreign exchange swap (FX swap) combining a spot conversion with a reverse forward for short-term liquidity parking of USD merchant receipts
Zero-cost collar built from a bought EUR call/USD put and sold EUR put/USD call, permitting the collectible card publisher to retain upside in USD appreciation while fixing a worst-case EUR rate
Participating forward allowing partial participation in favourable USD/EUR movement, suitable for the seasonal holiday peak of collector card sales
Deliverable EUR/CNH forward for offshore Renminbi payables to Chinese foil and holo-film suppliers, with settlement in EUR against CNH in the offshore market
Cross-currency interest rate swap (EUR/USD XCCY) for hedging the currency and interest-rate risk of medium-term intercompany loans from the parent treasury

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC) and net wealth tax (IFT) return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May following the end of the tax year (calendar-year entity); electronic filings through a tax agent are commonly extended to 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Taxation d'office (ex officio assessment); monthly late-payment interest of 0.6% (7.2% per annum); late-filing fines up to EUR 250,000 for bad-faith failure; criminal penalties for managing directors upon continued default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary annual general meeting of partners - approval of annual accounts and discharge of the gérant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed - minutes maintained in the statutory minute book at the registered office and made available to RCS/ACD inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of financial year end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct state fine; any partner may petition the Tribunal d'Arrondissement to convene the meeting; non-approval blocks timely RCS filing and exposes the gérant to liability for resulting penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes) including the independent auditor's report when audit thresholds are exceeded - deposit in the RCS with publication in the RESA electronic compendium
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) - Luxembourg Business Registers / eJustice portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of financial year end (by 31 July for a calendar-year SARL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice (mise en demeure); criminal fine from EUR 500 to EUR 25,000 for the gérant; publication of default in the RCS; prolonged non-filing may trigger court-ordered compliance, administrative strike-off and judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership in the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs - RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RBE unit under the Ministry of Justice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following each anniversary of the RBE registration; any UBO change resulting from share transfers must be reported within 1 month of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines from EUR 250 to EUR 1,250 per infraction imposed on the SARL and its gérant; verification and corrective enforcement by the RBE coordinator; repeated non-compliance may be escalated to criminal prosecution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint an independent statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises) if it exceeds two of three thresholds: balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million; net turnover above EUR 8.8 million; average workforce above 50 employees during the financial year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (LUX GAAP) per the Law of 19 December 2002, as amended, and the Code de commerce; EU-endorsed IFRS permitted for consolidated accounts and optional for standalone accounts of the unlisted SARL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must annually confirm the accuracy of its RBE filing within 30 days of the anniversary of its initial RBE registration. Any share/quota transfer that alters beneficial control, including crossing the 25% equity or voting-rights indicator, must be declared to the RBE within one month. The annual confirmation is submitted electronically through the LBR portal and is independent of the on-site register of members.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Register of Partners (Registre des associés) recording all quota holdings and transfers
Register of Managers / Directors (Registre des gérants)
Minute Book of shareholders' and management resolutions (Registre des procès-verbaux)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,000 - 22,000 per annum if compulsory audit thresholds are triggered; compilation/review-only engagements typically USD 3,000 - 8,000 if exempt
